title: Tri-region provisioning cadence and utilization vignettes
content:
Executive summary:
This working doc lays out three provisioning vignettes (conservative, baseline, aggressive) for NA / EU / APAC cloud regions covering GPU unit counts, targeted sustained utilization, and phased rollout cadence over the next 12 months. It's an infrastructure-facing planning sheet: not final procurement, but a concrete set of scenarios SRE/Capacity/Product can use to align Dedicated reservations and hosted autoscaling policies.

Assumptions (common across vignettes):
- Production request growth: host tokens/day +25% Q/Q baseline; bursty weekends for consumer apps.
- Average sustained per-GPU throughput (baseline model mix): 120k tokens/day on A100-80GB equivalency.
- Preferred hardware mix: H100 for latency-critical chat (capability premium); A100 for cost-sensitive batching; L7-class for embeddings/low-memory models.
- Warm pool target: 8–12% of regional fleet at any time; warm pool kept to minimize cold-start latency for Dedicated tenants.
- Priority routing: Dedicated reserved capacity -> Hosted local pool -> Cross-region spillover.

Scenarios (per region tables as compact vignettes):
1) Conservative (aim: minimize capital commitments)
- NA: Q2 add 80 A100-equivalent GPUs (seq windows: May 2026: +30, Jul 2026: +25, Sep 2026: +25); target sustained util 58%; warm pool 6%.
- EU: Q3 add 48 A100-equivalent GPUs (Aug 2026: +20, Oct 2026: +28); target util 62%; warm pool 6%.
- APAC: Q4 add 36 A100-equivalent GPUs (Nov 2026: +18, Jan 2027: +18); target util 64%; warm pool 8%.
Capex note: favors spot and short-term burst contracts; plan requires aggressive autoscale for spikes.

2) Baseline (preferred planning line)
- NA: Q2–Q4 incremental add 160 GPUs (May 40, Jun 40, Aug 40, Nov 40); target sustained util 65%; warm pool 10%.
- EU: phased 96 GPUs (Jun 24, Sep 24, Nov 24, Feb 24); target util 68%; warm pool 10%.
- APAC: phased 72 GPUs (Jul 18, Oct 18, Dec 18, Mar 18); target util 70%; warm pool 12%.
Operational impact: balances reserved capacity with some committed burst windows; improves latency SLOs for regional workloads.

3) Aggressive (aim: prioritize latency & headroom for enterprise demand)
- NA: immediate Q2 procurement +320 GPUs (large upfront), target util 50% (room for growth), warm pool 12%.
- EU: +180 GPUs across Q2/Q3, target util 52%, warm pool 12%.
- APAC: +150 GPUs across Q3/Q4, target util 54%, warm pool 14%.
Notes: requires negotiation for multi-year reservations; highest cost but lowest risk of cross-region spill and tail latency.

Rollout cadence & milestones (baseline mapping):
- March 2026: finalize vendor bids and SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L7). Owner: Asha.
- April 2026: confirm regional capacity target numbers and Dedicated customer allocation policy. Owner: Diego.
- May 2026: first tranche live in NA; capacity smoke tests, canary traffic for canary customers. Owner: Lin.
- Aug 2026: EU tranche live, conduct cross-region failover DR game day. Owner: Grace.
- Oct 2026: APAC tranche begins, enable local region routing and latency baselines. Owner: Michael.
- Ongoing: monthly utilization review, tagging of oversized instances for reclamation.

Triggers and gating criteria:
- Increase committed capacity if regional 7-day moving average sustained util >74% and 95th percentile latency degrades by >8% vs baseline.
- Pause procurement tranche if urgent SRE incidents >2 in tranche window or if hardware supply lead time grows >30% vs bid.
- Promote warm pool if model mix shifts toward long-sequence chat workloads (KV cache memory pressure >40%).

Operational details & caveats:
- Spillover policy: allow cross-region spill only when regional B/E capacity < 3% spare at 99th percentile demand. Prefer EU->NA as first spill target for latency-sensitive enterprise customers in NA/EU clusters depending on inter-region latency.
- Billing carveouts: Dedicated customers in early access get pinned physical capacity in the first 60 days of a tranche; after stabilization, policy moves to soft-pinning.
- Constraint: APAC cloud zones have longer vendor lead times (avg +3–6 weeks); factor into tranche timing.

Risks & mitigations:
- Supply shock: maintain a 4-week tactical buffer using cloud burst partners and short-term spot pools.
- Over-provisioning (cost): introduce monthly reclaim cadence and automated right-sizing alerts for underutilized PINs.
- Latency regression after rollout: attach telemetry flagging to per-model slowdowns; automatic rollback to previous model-variant if 99th percentile latency rises >12%.

Open questions / deferred items:
- Exact hardware splits per tranche (H100 % vs A100 %) — needs inputs from research on seq-length mix.
- How to charge internal product teams for warm pool reserved overhead — billing model proposal pending (finance/chargeback).
- SLA perimeter changes for Dedicated tiers after region expansion — legal & sales input needed.

Action items (next 30d):
- Run a sensitivity analysis for token growth +10% / +20% / +40% and produce a simple table mapping to incremental GPUs needed (Lin).
- Start vendor RFP (shortlist 3) with supply lead times and price escalation clauses (Asha).
- Draft customer communication template for tranche rollouts and potential temporary throttling during canary windows (Grace).

Notes to self / informal:
- If APAC procurement stalls, consider temporary cross-region cache warmers to reduce cold-start token cost.
- Remember to add an eval run for the new quantized model profile; lower mem footprint could change target util.
